newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican political, pension fund ads boost Televisa.
newsitem.headline: Mexican political, pension fund ads boost Televisa.

text.p: Political campaigning and pension fund advertising boosted second quarter revenues from television commercials at Mexico's Televisa by 24.6 percent over the year-ago quarter, the company said late Wednesday.
Television sales, representing 59.3 percent of total company sales, rose to 1.962 billion pesos in the second quarter, Televisa said.

Latin America's largest television company said it benefitted from the heavy media play ahead of the July 6 elections as well as from competition among financial institutions trying to draw workers into the newly privatized pension system.

"This increase primarily reflects revenues from sales of advertising under the company's French Plan (particularly increases from political campaigns and pension funds)," Televisa said in a statement.
Under the French Plan, Televisa has advertisers pay the following year's advertising ahead of time, usually in the fall.
The recent elections were considered the cleanest in Mexico's history. Voters elected most of a new Congress, six state governors and, for the first time this century, the mayor of Mexico City.
